# tacsim's integration test targets and the CI cells that run them
# (.github/workflows/ci.yml's `tacsim-integration-N`; scripts/ci-tacsim-shard.sh N).
#
# Since doc 43 cut TS.12's adoption (D-43-5, 2026-11-04) tacsim's tests are
# four DOMAIN binaries, `crates/tacsim/tests/<domain>.rs` with their modules
# under `tests/<domain>/`, and every cell builds all four and runs its share
# of their tests. A new test is a `mod` line in its domain root, never a line
# here.
#
# The share is planned by measured time (2026-11-18), not by hash. Until then
# it was `cargo nextest run --partition hash:N/10`, and the hash put the slow
# 512-site field stories together: over main's green runs 44171357746,
# 44195103450, 44207692403, 44223456939 and 44362324881 cell 6 summed 73-96
# test-minutes (s2_the_field_story_at_512, su3_a_restart_redraws_nothing_at_512,
# su5_an_unloaded_yield_lapses_after_28_ic_days, ap4a, mw14a_at_512 and ap8,
# 22 minutes of it) against a mean of 57, and was the run's wall at 18-29 min.
# Now scripts/tacsim-cells.py lists the tests every cell would run and places
# them longest first, each onto the least-loaded cell: the `weight:` lines
# below at their seconds, every other test at the `default-weight:`. Every
# cell computes the same plan from the same list, so each test runs once.
# Replayed on those five runs (weights from four, times from the fifth), the
# heaviest cell came to 1.04-1.10x the median.
#
# Keeping it balanced: a slow test with no `weight:` line is placed at the
# default, so new slow stories drift the cells apart again. Refresh the lines
# from three to five recent green main runs:
#   gh run download <run> -p 'nextest-junit-tacsim-integration-*' -D junit/<run>
#   python3 scripts/tacsim-cells.py weights junit/*
# and paste its output over the `default-weight:` and `weight:` lines (every
# test whose mean is at least 60 s). A weight for a test that no longer exists
# is a guard failure (`ci_tacsim_shards`); a renamed test falls back to the
# default until the next refresh. Each cell's log prints the plan
# ("planned test-minutes").
#
# The `partition:` line names the planned binaries. A numbered line
# `N: target ...` names the targets cell N runs FIRST, by name and whole,
# before its share (an empty line runs none); a `weight:` line naming a whole
# target is its cost to its cell in test-thread seconds, which the plan
# starts that cell's load from:
# - harness stays a target of its own (its `#![recursion_limit]` is
#   crate-root-only) and is cell 1's.
# - cost_lane runs alone (.config/nextest.toml: threads-required = the whole
#   pool) and is cell 2's, so its serial minutes sit on one cell, first,
#   rather than stalling all ten. Its 3.5-6.6 min of wall hold the pool's four
#   threads, so its weight is four times its mean wall of 294 s.
# Every top-level `tests/*.rs` target appears exactly once in this file
# (`ci_tacsim_shards` is the guard), and the workflow's matrix runs exactly
# the numbered cells.
partition: domain_arena domain_economy domain_field domain_world
1: harness
2: cost_lane

weight: 1176 cost_lane
default-weight: 10.5
